question: What filesystem boundary should OpenClaw expose: a `tools.fs` allow/deny PathGuard policy, a `tools.fs.roots` access-mode policy, or a narrower workspace-only/exec-split design?
rationale: This defines a public config surface and security boundary, and the current open PRs show competing designs with different compatibility and false-security tradeoffs.

options.title: Settle one `tools.fs` path-policy contract
options.body: Choose a canonical config shape, require normalization/symlink/deny precedence tests, and make exec coverage explicit before merging either implementation path.

options.title: Split exec into a separate tracker
options.body: Land a file-tool-only policy only if docs and labels state that shell-mediated file access remains a separate security boundary.

options.title: Defer to OS/container isolation
options.body: Close or downgrade the config request only if maintainers decide OpenClaw should not own host filesystem path ACLs beyond workspaceOnly and sandbox backends.

recommendation.title: Settle one `tools.fs` path-policy contract
recommendation.body: Choose a canonical config shape, require normalization/symlink/deny precedence tests, and make exec coverage explicit before merging either implementation path.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already framed the prior keep-open review and has the strongest current history on the config/schema and workspaceOnly security path.
